scope: Research and independent mathematical adaptations of seven non-MSA/non-MERC conditioning/recalibration papers for one OSRAM readout. No original benchmark reproduction or copied implementation.

common_contract.tokens: X[N,5,D], fixed slots [Local,Base,GapA,GapT,GapV], D=128 after the shared wrapper's projections; active[N,5] is boolean.
common_contract.boundary: No new memory scan, memory update, temporal query, cache, loss, or train/test mask. Modules see only one utterance's five tokens. The parent wrapper owns the zero-initialized output projection to the existing Flat width.
common_contract.masking: Remove inactive values using torch.where before arithmetic; mask biased slot transformations afterwards; mean/max/variance exclude inactive slots; all-inactive rows return exact zero.
common_contract.axes: Convolution in ECA operates on feature channels; convolution in CBAM operates only on the five fixed typed slots. Neither sees utterance/time indices. No BatchNorm, dropout, random operations, or sample mixing in forward.
common_contract.interpretation: All OSRAM constructions below are adaptations. Published gains concern visual tasks and do not establish an OSRAM benefit. Existing failed gates must remain baselines; identical functions under new names do not count as new methods.

verification_summary.notes: SK original repository and raw model URL return HTTP 404; original source is recoverable from a GitHub-confirmed fork, and a coauthor hosts an explicitly modified dense/grouped SK-ResNet variant. License absence is recorded rather than inferred.

papers.title: FiLM: Visual Reasoning with a General Conditioning Layer
papers.method_evidence: Section 2.1, equations (1)-(2): a conditioner predicts independent feature-wise scale and shift.
papers.official_evidence: The AAAI paper names ethanjperez/film, whose README identifies this as its reproduction code.

license.note: Repository text explicitly names Attribution-NonCommercial 4.0 International; no code copied.

papers.original_formula: gamma=f(c), beta=h(c); FiLM(F|c)=gamma(c) elementwise_mul F + beta(c).

adaptation.changed: Replace language GRU/image features with a current-Local conditioner and four memory-read tokens; retain affine scale plus shift. No normalization or temporal conditioning.
adaptation.limitation: Affine shift can change an active zero-valued token; it is a readout offset, not recovered modality evidence. Inactive tokens remain zero.
adaptation.duplicate_risk: High if reduced to scale-only sigmoid gating; compare explicitly with existing availability-affine and local/history gates.
adaptation.relevance: Moderate; useful as an established affine-conditioning control, not a new contribution.

papers.title: Squeeze-and-Excitation Networks
papers.method_evidence: Section 3, equations (2)-(4). Version v2 matches the three-author CVPR paper; later arXiv/journal versions add authors.

code_files.symbol: conv2_1_global_pool -> conv2_1_1x1_down -> ReLU -> conv2_1_1x1_up -> Sigmoid -> Axpy

papers.official_evidence: CVPR paper directly links this author Caffe repository.

license.note: Verified root license; no code copied.

papers.original_formula: z_c=mean_spatial(U_c); s=sigmoid(W2 ReLU(W1 z)); U'_c=s_c U_c.

adaptation.changed: The squeeze axis is five projected evidence types, not image pixels. A shared channel weight rescales all active slots.
adaptation.limitation: No spatial evidence exists here; this is a small evidence-pooling adaptation. The excitation can be a generic MLP gate already tested in the project.
adaptation.duplicate_risk: Very high; count as an established SE control only after checking functional overlap with prior gates.
adaptation.relevance: Low-to-moderate as a diagnostic baseline; not inherently a new mechanism.

papers.title: ECA-Net: Efficient Channel Attention for Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.method_evidence: Section 3.2.2 equation (9) and Section 3.2.3: shared local channel interaction without an MLP bottleneck.
papers.official_evidence: Author repository README cites the matching ECA-Net paper and provides its models.

license.note: Verified root license; no code copied.

papers.original_formula: z=GAP(X); w=sigmoid(Conv1D_k(z)); X'=X*w; kernel spans adjacent channel descriptors.

fixed_hyperparameters.kernel_rule: t=floor(abs((log2(D)+1)/2)); k=t if odd else t+1

adaptation.changed: Only the squeeze axis changes to active evidence slots. The convolution remains over feature coordinates, never utterance positions.
adaptation.limitation: Neighboring learned coordinates lack a guaranteed semantic locality; channel ordering is an inductive assumption.
adaptation.duplicate_risk: Lower than generic MLP gating only if the shared banded channel operator is retained.
adaptation.relevance: Moderate; very small, structurally distinct channel-interaction control.

papers.title: CBAM: Convolutional Block Attention Module
papers.method_evidence: Section 3 equations (1)-(3): sequential channel then spatial attention; shared MLP for average and maximum descriptors.
papers.official_evidence: Repository explicitly identifies itself as official PyTorch code for CBAM and BAM.

license.note: Verified root license; no code copied.

adaptation.formula: Use masked mean/max over five slots for Mc; then concatenate per-slot feature mean/max and apply Conv1D(kernel=7) over the fixed five slots for Ms; mask slots and average.
adaptation.changed: Replace two image axes by the fixed evidence-slot axis; remove official spatial-branch BatchNorm to avoid batch mixing. No time axis is available.
adaptation.limitation: Typed-slot adjacency is arbitrary. Applying unmodified CBAM to a 1x1 vector degenerates its spatial component; this construction is explicitly different from original CBAM.
adaptation.duplicate_risk: High if either stage is omitted; keep shared avg/max channel MLP and the separate current-slot gate to distinguish the control.

papers.title: Gated Channel Transformation for Visual Recognition
papers.method_evidence: Section 3 equations (2)-(5), Figure 3: L2 embedding, channel normalization, identity-centered tanh scaling.
papers.official_evidence: Author repository README identifies TensorFlow and PyTorch implementations of the CVPR paper.

license.note: No root/PyTorch license detected; do not infer the subtree license covers PyTorch. Independent formulas only.

adaptation.formula: Sum squared values only over active evidence slots, normalize across D channels, scale each active token, masked-average the result.
adaptation.changed: The original spatial reduction becomes a within-utterance slot reduction. Identity initialization and 3D channel parameters are retained.
adaptation.limitation: Magnitude-based scaling is not a reliability estimator. Repository training advice on gating-bias weight decay is not imported into the fixed OSRAM optimizer.
adaptation.duplicate_risk: Moderate; distinguish exact L2-normalized 3-vector operator from arbitrary MLP/tanh gates and existing GRN.
adaptation.relevance: Moderate; compact normalization-based recalibration with explicit identity initialization.

papers.title: SimAM: A Simple, Parameter-Free Attention Module for Convolutional Neural Networks
papers.method_evidence: Section 3 equations (5)-(6) and Figure 3. Code uses M-1 variance denominator.
papers.official_evidence: Repository explicitly identifies the official PyTorch implementation of the ICML paper.

license.note: Recursive repository tree and relevant file contain no detected LICENSE/COPYING declaration. Independent formulas only.

adaptation.formula: For each feature channel compute mean/variance over active slots only; apply the inverse-energy weight to each active token, then masked-mean. If fewer than two slots are active, use identity.
adaptation.changed: Evidence types replace spatial neurons. Singleton identity is a necessary explicit adaptation: official code divides by zero at H*W=1.
adaptation.limitation: Five heterogeneous token types do not satisfy an established common spatial-neuron distribution. With two active slots, symmetric deviations can make weights identical; no learned selector is added.
adaptation.duplicate_risk: Low structural overlap with learned gates, but any learned MLP would cease to be this parameter-free control.
adaptation.relevance: Low; useful cheap negative/control case, not strong transfer evidence.

papers.title: Selective Kernel Networks
papers.method_evidence: Section 3.1 equations (1)-(6): multiple spatial receptive-field branches, pooled descriptor, per-channel branch softmax and weighted fusion.

code_files.symbol: conv2_1/3x3g32 and conv2_1/3x3g32d2; B_global_pool; B_fc1; branch softmax

papers.official_evidence: Original paper names implus/SKNet. GitHub API for roy-wong-d24h/SKNet identifies parent and source as implus/SKNet; snapshot commit 17dd7086d4959be0c8c6ccce52e4fd8187836770 is authored by xiangli (2019-03-26). Coauthor repository README explicitly calls SK-ResNet a modified version.

license.note: No root license detected in preserved original-source tree or coauthor mirror; no source copied.

papers.original_formula: U=sum_m U_m; z=ReLU(BN(W*GAP(U))); a_m,c=softmax_m(A_m z)_c; V_c=sum_m a_m,c U_m,c.

adaptation.formula: U_m,i=where(active_i,ReLU(W_m Xi+b_m),0), m=1,2; z=ReLU(W*masked_mean(U1+U2)+b); a=softmax_over_branches(A_m z+b_m); output=masked_mean(sum_m a_m*U_m).
adaptation.changed: Dense D->D channel transformations replace multiscale spatial kernels; BatchNorm removed. Retain separate transformed branches, shared fused descriptor, and per-channel branch competition.
adaptation.limitation: This is dense SK-inspired branch selection, not SK convolution or original SKNet reproduction; receptive-field adaptivity is absent. Direct official repository access remains a provenance gap.
adaptation.duplicate_risk: High if branches become raw Local/Base/Gap weights or scalar gates. Keep two distinct channel transforms and per-channel branch softmax.
adaptation.relevance: Moderate as a branch-selection control; not evidence of a new memory/readout contribution.
